title: Theo and the Witness Anew
premise: Isandro Blackwood, a night-shift taxi dispatcher in the fading town of Marrow Creek, has spent fifteen years cataloguing secrets instead of living his own. When a missing woman's diary surfaces with entries dated after her disappearance, he realizes the town's oldest closed case was never closed at all. Following the diary's coded routes through his own dispatch logs, Isandro uncovers a thirty-year-old cover-up implicating the town's founding families—and discovers Theo, the missing woman's son, has been alive all along, hidden by the very people who swore she died. In the end, Isandro must choose between exposing the truth and protecting Theo, and finds a third path: letting the town convict itself, one archived secret at a time.
about_author: Juniper Reyes is a former small-town court stenographer who spent a decade transcribing other people's confessions before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about quiet people who keep dangerous records, from a farmhouse office that smells of ink and rain.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Absences
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. A slow night shift establishes Isandro's ritualized, invisible life: filing ride logs, memorizing the town's rhythms, avoiding human connection. He receives an anonymous package containing a diary belonging to Lena Voss, missing fifteen years. Emotional beat: loneliness cracked open by curiosity.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Reading by lamplight, he discovers the diary continues three weeks past Lena's disappearance date, written in her hand. The final entry names a pickup address—a house that burned down decades ago. Emotional beat: dread blooming into obsession.

chapters.title: Dispatch Log 1998
chapters.summary: POV Isandro, with flashback texture. He pulls fifteen-year-old cab records and finds a fare logged to the burned house on the night Lena vanished—under a name that doesn't exist. Someone used his company as an alibi machine. Emotional beat: betrayal.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Wasn't Mourned
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. He visits Lena's sister, Delia, who mentions a son, Theo, taken in by the Hollis family after the disappearance. The boy never appeared in any record Isandro can find. Emotional beat: grief for a child erased.

chapters.title: Theo
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Introduced in present day as a reclusive handyman at the Hollis estate, Theo recognizes the diary when Isandro shows it around town. He lies badly about not knowing it. Emotional beat: terror of being seen.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibis
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Cross-referencing old logs, he maps how the town's leading families traded cab fares like currency to build perfect alibis for the night Lena disappeared. Emotional beat: the horror of systemic complicity.

chapters.title: What Delia Buried
chapters.summary: POV Delia. Her chapter reveals she found evidence years ago and chose silence to keep custody of Theo's memory intact—or so she tells herself. She warns Isandro off. Emotional beat: guilt wearing the mask of protection.

chapters.title: The Burned House
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. He and Theo, uneasy allies now, search the ruins of the address in the diary and find a child's tin box buried beneath the floorboards: photographs, a key, and a page torn from the diary. Emotional beat: fragile trust.

chapters.title: Key to the Hollis Wing
chapters.summary: POV Theo. The key fits a locked room in the Hollis mansion where Theo grew up. Inside: boxes of files labeled with cab fare numbers. His foster father, Aldous Hollis, catches him at the door. Emotional beat: the past as captor.

chapters.title: Aldous Explains Nothing
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Aldous offers Isandro money and a warning, revealing he knows about the diary. He claims Lena left town alive and the diary entries after are forged. Emotional beat: menace dressed as civility.

chapters.title: Handwriting
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Consulting a retired graphologist, Isandro confirms the post-disappearance entries are genuine—but written under duress, the letters cramped and hurried. Lena was alive and captive. Emotional beat: hope curdling into urgency.

chapters.title: The Route She Memorized
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Decoding the diary's street references, Theo realizes Lena mapped her own captivity using landmarks only a dispatcher would recognize—she was leaving a trail for someone like Isandro. Emotional beat: awe at his mother's cunning.

chapters.title: Someone Follows the Logs
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. His office is ransacked; the original 1998 logbook is gone. A colleague, Marta, admits she was paid to copy records for Aldous years ago. Emotional beat: paranoia, then unexpected alliance.

chapters.title: Delia Breaks
chapters.summary: POV Delia. Confronted with the tin box photos, Delia confesses: she saw Lena alive weeks after the disappearance and stayed silent because Aldous threatened Theo. Emotional beat: shame finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: The Third Fare
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Reconstructing the night, Isandro identifies a third unlogged fare—the driver who took Lena away and never reported back. That driver was young Aldous himself. Emotional beat: the case snapping shut.

chapters.title: Run, Theo
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Aldous, cornered, tries to have Theo committed under an old conservatorship paper—the mechanism used to erase him as a child. Theo flees through the town he was hidden in. Emotional beat: flight as defiance.

chapters.title: Night Shift Siege
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Using the dispatch system, Isandro tracks every cab in town to shield Theo, rerouting Aldous's men with false calls. The town's surveillance network turns against its owners. Emotional beat: competence as courage.

chapters.title: Where She Waited
chapters.summary: POV Isandro and Theo. The diary's final decoded route leads to a storm cellar outside town—Lena's last hiding place. They find her remains and, beside them, a finished confession naming every conspirator. Emotional beat: mourning and vindication entwined.

chapters.title: The Town Convicts Itself
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Rather than hand everything to the corrupt sheriff, Isandro mails copies of the archive to every household in Marrow Creek. The town erupts; alibis unravel publicly; Aldous is arrested by state police. Emotional beat: justice outside the law.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: POV Theo. At the preliminary hearing, Theo testifies about the locked room and the erased boy he was. Delia corroborates. The conservatorship papers are struck down. Emotional beat: reclaiming a name.

chapters.title: What Memory Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Weeks later, Isandro buries the diary with Lena's remains and keeps only one page—the route she drew for him. He begins, tentatively, to live visibly: daylight, neighbors, Marta's coffee. Emotional beat: grief settling into purpose.

chapters.title: Witness Anew
chapters.summary: POV Theo, closing frame. Theo takes a job at the dispatch office, learning the alphabet of the town so no one can be filed away and forgotten again. The last line mirrors the diary's first. Emotional beat: witness renewed, cycle broken.
